readme:
# Asyntai AI Assistant for Backstage

Give your engineers an AI assistant inside your Backstage developer portal.
They ask a question in plain words and get an answer from the content you gave
[Asyntai](https://asyntai.com): your documentation site, your runbooks, your
internal guides. Answers come with links to the right page, in the language of
the question.

![The AI Assistant page in Backstage](docs/screenshot.png)

## What you get

- An **AI Assistant** page with its own item in the sidebar
- An **Ask AI** card for the Backstage home page
- Follow-up questions in the same conversation, and a **New chat** button
- A knowledge base picker when your Asyntai account has more than one website
- Answers with headings, lists and links, in more than 80 languages
- Works with the new frontend system and the legacy one

## Requirements

- Backstage with `@backstage/core-components` 0.18 or newer
- An Asyntai account on the Starter plan or higher, because the plugin uses the
  Asyntai API

## Install

From the root of your Backstage repository:

```bash
yarn --cwd packages/app add @asyntai/backstage-plugin-ai-assistant
```

### 1. Add the API key

Sign in to Asyntai, open **Settings**, then **API**, and copy your API key.
Store it on your Backstage server as the environment variable
`ASYNTAI_API_KEY`.

### 2. Add the proxy entry

Add this to `app-config.yaml`. The Backstage backend adds the key to each
request, so the key never reaches the browser.

```yaml
proxy:
  endpoints:
    /asyntai:
      target: https://asyntai.com
      headers:
        Authorization: Bearer ${ASYNTAI_API_KEY}
      allowedMethods: ['GET', 'POST']
```

### 3a. New frontend system

Nothing more to do when feature discovery is on (`app.packages: all`). The
**AI Assistant** page appears in the sidebar at `/ai-assistant`.

Without feature discovery, add the plugin to `packages/app/src/App.tsx`:

```tsx
import asyntaiPlugin from '@asyntai/backstage-plugin-ai-assistant';

export default createApp({
  features: [/* your other features */, asyntaiPlugin],
});
```

The plugin also brings a home page widget called **Ask AI**
(`AsyntaiAskAi`). Add it from the home page editor, or list it in the
`page:home` default layout in `app-config.yaml`:

```yaml
app:
  extensions:
    - page:home:
        config:
          defaultConfig:
            - component: AsyntaiAskAi
              column: 0
              row: 0
              width: 6
              height: 6
```

### 3b. Legacy frontend system

Add a route in `packages/app/src/App.tsx`:

```tsx
import { AsyntaiAssistantPage } from '@asyntai/backstage-plugin-ai-assistant';

<Route path="/ai-assistant" element={<AsyntaiAssistantPage />} />
```

Add a sidebar item in `packages/app/src/components/Root/Root.tsx`:

```tsx
import { AsyntaiIcon } from '@asyntai/backstage-plugin-ai-assistant';

<SidebarItem icon={AsyntaiIcon} to="ai-assistant" text="AI Assistant" />
```

To put the card on your home page or any other page:

```tsx
import { AsyntaiAssistantCard } from '@asyntai/backstage-plugin-ai-assistant';

<AsyntaiAssistantCard />
```

## Options

All options are optional:

```yaml
asyntai:
  websiteId: docs.example.com   # a website id or domain from your Asyntai account
  title: Engineering Assistant  # the page title
  proxyPath: /asyntai           # change it only if you renamed the proxy entry
```

Without `websiteId`, the plugin uses your primary website and shows a picker
when the account has more than one. The page and the card also take a
`websiteId` prop, which wins over the config.
